sweep_summary: Southeastern Nochixtlán Mixtec (sout3002, mxy) is not in the catalog. The single works with stress in the title, McKendry's 2013 Edinburgh PhD thesis, was already held by the project in with a text layer and was re-read page by page; the companion 2001 UND MA sketch is also there. The thesis is a first-hand, instrumentally supported account: one primary stress per word on the initial syllable of the root (or the only syllable of a heavy monosyllable), prefixes/clitics never stressed, second root stressed in compounds, no secondary stress, no tone-stress correlation (Ch. 9 Exp. 1: initial vowel longer, F(1,3)=13.5, p=0.03, and more intense, F(1,3)=17.07, p=0.03). This is a ready-to-code statement for a new catalog record: fixed initial stress at root level (with prefixes outside the stress domain). Nothing remains to acquire; the CORE download URL was re-checked live and was updated with verified page/PDF locators.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tone language (H/M/L with floating tones); word stress is predictable and non-contrastive: it falls on the initial syllable of the (bimoraic) root, i.e. a single trochaic foot ('CV.CV) or ('CV:) built over the root; prefixes (e.g. animal classifier tʃi-, verbal prefixes) are never stressed, so prefixed words surface with penultimate = root-initial stress; in root+root compounds only the second root is stressed (on its initial syllable). Acoustic correlates: greater duration and intensity of the root-initial vowel; stress placement is independent of tone (High tones are not attracted to the stressed syllable).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Author states explicitly there is only primary stress in MXY (one stressed syllable per word; no secondary stress, no stressed affixes).
new_statements.exceptions: A root is unstressed when it is the first element of a compound; roots (e.g. verbs used as auxiliaries, or when a noun is in contrastive focus) may be de-accented when the focus of the utterance is elsewhere; status of tuku 'again' (stressed only under focus?) left open (sec. 11.4.7). Spanish loans keep stress-related tone patterns (H on the Spanish stressed syllable).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (prosodic word = root plus prefixes/enclitics); evidence from nouns and verbs in carrier sentences under information vs contrastive focus; descriptive data mainly from the Santo Domingo Nuxaá sub-variety.
new_statements.identity_note: McKendry's MXY = the closely related varieties of Santo Domingo Nuxaá, San Andrés Nuxiño and Santa Inés de Zaragoza (district of Nochixtlán, Oaxaca); the descriptive and recorded data focus on the Santo Domingo Nuxaá sub-variety (thesis p. 131, fn. 1 p. 1). This matches Glottolog sout3002 / ISO mxy directly.

new_statements.reading: Fixed initial (root-initial) stress: the first syllable of the bimoraic root carries the single primary stress; prefixes and clitics are unstressed; in compounds the second root's initial syllable is stressed; monosyllabic heavy words stress their only syllable; no secondary stress; High tone does not attract stress (acoustic evidence: longer and more intense initial vowel, no tone effect). Variety: MXY, chiefly Santo Domingo Nuxaá (Nochixtlán district, Oaxaca).
